newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries start weaker pre-durables, auctions.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries start weaker pre-durables, auctions.

text.p: U.S. Treasury securities started on a weak footing, dragged down after European bonds dipped on French election worries.

"In Japan, I guess there was a little bit of buying, net, net ... but then when they started taking Europe apart we went with it," said Mead Briggs, proprietary trading manager at Credit Suisse First Boston.
Briggs said the two-year and five-year notes were hurt more than bonds, in the run up to the Treasury's auction of $16.5 billion in twos on Wednesday.
But before the auction the market will have time to digest economic data, the most important of which is April durable goods, due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.

Durable goods are expected to have risen 1.3 percent, according to economists polled by Reuters. The rise would follow a 2.6 percent decline in March. Ex-defense, durables are seen up 0.8 percent, after a 2.3 percent fall previously.
At 0900 EDT/1300 GMT comes BTM/Schroders weekly chain store sales for the week ending May 24. Sales rose 0.3 percent the previous week.
The market remained nervous after the yield on the 30-year bond pushed above 7.0 percent on Tuesday, on the back of a surprisingly robust reading on consumer confidence in May.
Traders said that yields on the two- and five-year issues may have room to back up further to draw in more buyers, before the Treasury starts accepting bids for the two-year at 1300 EDT.

"The market sold off pretty good yesterday. We're probably also going to see continued weakness in the front end of the curve," said Greg Carr, bond market analyst at A.G. Edwards and Sons Inc, adding the market will "set up negative."
The Treasury was slated to sell $12 billion in five-year notes on Thursday.
U.S. bond prices probed higher overnight, mostly on the back of swap activity, particularly in the 10-year sector, bond experts said.

But Treasuries were pulled lower again in tandem with European bonds, which slipped on rumors that opinion polls in France showed the left-leaning parties well-placed for a second-round victory in the parliamentary election on Sunday.
In early trade on Wednesday, the T-bond was up 4/32 at 95-4/32, yielding 7.02 percent. The 10-year note was up 1/32 at 98-27/32, with a yield of 6.79 percent.
At the short end of the coupon sector the two-year note was unchanged at 100-5/32, yielding 6.28 percent and the five-year was unchanged at 99-31/32, yielding 6.63 percent.
In bills, the three-month was down one basis point at 5.03 percent and the six-month was unchanged at 5.26 percent. The year bill was up one basis point at 5.55 percent.
